title: Origin scaling kernels for symplectic Mittag-Leffler ensembles with reciprocal-integer radial exponent and point charge c>-1
author: Gernot Akemann; Sung-Soo Byun; Nam-Gyu Kang
source_title: Scaling Limits of Planar Symplectic Ensembles
difficulty_reason: The proof derives a new Christoffel-Darboux differential system directly from the gamma-product double series of skew-orthogonal polynomials. It establishes the compact-uniform scaling kernel and solves the resulting integer-order inhomogeneous equation using a Mittag-Leffler fundamental system. An explicit Wronskian normalization and beta-integral coefficient identity remove every homogeneous contribution, yielding the full antisymmetric integral kernel.
source_version: Official SIGMA 18 (2022) article 007, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2022.007; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The full Theorem2.4 and Proposition4.1 core are included, restricted to lambda=1/m, m a positive integer, with c>-1 and Q(zeta)=|zeta|^(2/m)-(2c/N)log|zeta|, at the singular origin with the exact micro-scale(2.13). Existing radial skew-polynomial/Pfaffian representation theory and the standard Mittag-Leffler homogeneous solutions are background; the new gamma-product system, scaling and inhomogeneous normalization are supplied. Arbitrary fractional-order claims of4.1 are only context, not a separate selected result. The author permits branch changes as cocycles preserving correlation functions; no single-valued pre-kernel is asserted. The proof last displayed line keeps a tilde W symbol after extracting F although(4.14) defines that tilde as already containing F. Preserve this local display literally with the editorial note: the preceding integral formula and explicit(4.14) give the claimed statement without any missing core or replacement argument.
